title: SAT Math 9 — Statistics and Probability Quiz
question: Five SAT-style questions on statistics and probability, with full working.
intro: Five questions on statistics and probability. **Show your working before you choose or type an answer.**

questions.title: A sixth number
questions.prompt:
The mean of five numbers is 14.

A sixth number is added, and the mean of the six numbers is 15. What is the sixth number?

questions.title: Compare the spread
questions.prompt:
Set A: 40, 45, 50, 55, 60

Set B: 48, 49, 50, 51, 52

Which statement is true?
choices: The means are equal, and set B has the larger standard deviation.
Set A has the larger mean and the larger standard deviation.
The means are equal, and set A has the larger standard deviation.
The means and the standard deviations are equal.
questions.solution: Both sets are symmetric about 50, so both means are 50. Set A's values lie 5 to 10 from 50; set B's lie 1 to 2 from 50. Set A is more spread out: **larger standard deviation**.

questions.title: Margin of error
questions.prompt:
A random sample of 500 voters in one city found that 46% support a new park. The margin of error is 3%.

Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Exactly 46% of the city's voters support the park.
It is plausible that between 43% and 49% of the city's voters support the park.
Between 43% and 49% of all voters in the country support the park.
A larger sample would make the margin of error larger.
questions.solution: \(46\% \pm 3\%\) gives 43% to 49%, and it describes the **city** (where the sample came from), not the country. A larger sample makes the margin smaller.

questions.title: Given the sum
questions.prompt:
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled.

Given that the sum is 8, what is the probability that at least one die shows a 3?
questions.solution_title: List only the outcomes with sum 8
questions.solution:
Sum 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2). That is 5 outcomes.

With a 3: (3,5) and (5,3). That is 2 outcomes.

\[P = \boxed{\tfrac{2}{5}}\]

\(\tfrac{1}{18}\) divides by all 36 outcomes, ignoring “given that”.

questions.title: Residual from a line of fit
questions.prompt:
A line of best fit for a scatterplot is

\[y = 1.8x + 32\]

One data point is \((25, 74)\). What is the residual for this point?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} \hat{y} &= 1.8(25) + 32 \\ &= 77 \end{aligned}\]

\[\begin{aligned} \text{residual} &= 74 - 77 \\ &= \boxed{-3} \end{aligned}\]

Negative: the line overestimates this point.

takeaway: Turn means into sums, condition by shrinking the denominator, generalise only to the sampled population, and residual = actual − predicted.
